eligibility.quote: On Ubuntu 24.04, maximum speed is limited to \~0.25 m/s.

failed_conditions.quote: Fixes a Humble to Jazzy regression: MPPI seeds rollouts from lagging odometry instead of its own last command

loudness.quote: On Ubuntu 24.04, maximum speed is limited to \~0.25 m/s.

resolution.quote: and it is effective in JAZZY. It seems that the small acceleration value causes the vehicle to slow down.

notes: Verified via gh api: issue #5386 body (title 'MPPI Controller same YAML reaches 0.8 m/s on ROS2 Humble but only 0.25 m/s on ROS2 Jazzy', version 'ros-jazzy-navigation2 1.3.7-1noble.20250624.020544', and the ~0.25 m/s sentence at body line 260/266) and its comments (reporter's closing diagnosis and the other user's ax_max 15.0 workaround), and PR #6336 'Backport #5617 to Jazzy' with the regression bullet, merged 2026-08-11 as 3f71f94b, tested on a MuJoCo Ridgeback (a different peer). Loudness disagree: the spec labels the case loud_documented while its own loudness_evidence says 'no diagnostic is reported, the reporter found it by observing /cmd_vel'; the quoted sentence is an observed wrong-motion symptom, not a diagnostic from existing tooling at build/connection/activation, so the case is silent_documented at run. Eligibility agreed with the spec's low confidence: the failure depends on a cross-unit timing assumption (odometry twist lagging the last command), though the reporter's own reading (Jazzy newly enforcing the acceleration parameters in the same node's YAML) would be an internal/config reading; the spec followed the merged fix's attribution, which is the primary-source statement of the mechanism.
